description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of ethical principles within a medical context. The chart contains 16 distinct slices, each representing a different principle. The slices are labeled with terms such as “Recognize the Responsibility of the Occupation,” “Justice,” “Beneficence,” “Autonomy,” “Non-Maleficence,” “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally,” “Continual Learning,” “Provide Assistance in Emergency,” “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Give Top Priority to Patient’s Interest,” “Ethical Research,” “Minimizing Conflicts of Interest,” and a series of more detailed principles related to patient rights and professional conduct. The slices are colored in shades of green, ranging from light to dark, and appear to be ordered visually by decreasing size, with “Beneficence” occupying the largest proportion. The chart includes a legend identifying each principle and its corresponding color, and percentage labels are not present within the slices themselves. No slices are visually emphasized through techniques like exploding or bolding.
